Conversation Memory & Intent Modeling System

## Overview
Two-layer enhancement to the existing memory infrastructure: (1) full conversation transcript embedding pipeline, and (2) decision-preference modeling that generalizes from corrections/approvals into predictive intent understanding.

## Feature 1: Transcript Embedding Pipeline
- Post-session hook that chunks full conversation transcripts and stores embeddings via OpenMemory
- Semantic retrieval at session start ("what has the user said about X") pulls actual conversation fragments
- behavioral-prefs.md becomes a cache over richer underlying data, not the sole copy
- Uses existing Ollama nomic-embed-text infrastructure
- Stop hook integration: after existing correction extraction, chunk and embed the full transcript

## Feature 2: Decision Preference Modeling  
- Lightweight tagging system for decisions made during sessions (routing, scope, communication, architecture)
- Signal capture from user responses: corrections = negative signal, approvals/silence = positive signal
- Preference model that generalizes beyond exact-match rules
- Query interface: "given this decision type, what would the user likely prefer?"
- Builds on existing corrections.md and behavioral-prefs.md pipeline

## Technical constraints
- All storage in ~/.claude/.claude/ (existing OpenMemory sqlite + new tables or collections)
- Ollama embeddings already available locally
- Stop hook is the integration point for post-session processing
- Must not break existing session start/stop flow
- Python preferred (consistent with mcp-servers/gemini/ codebase)
